props.gloss_en: the mishna: kodashim inside -- the first is fit and he is exempt; for the second he receives forty, and it is unfit
the mishna: kodashim outside -- for the first he is liable karet, both are unfit, and for both he receives forty
stam: let him also be flogged [for the second, kodashim inside] for the prohibition of an animal lacking time
baraita: from where that all the disqualifications of ox and sheep are under 'it shall not be accepted'? 'an ox or a sheep that has a limb too long or too short' (Lev 22:23) taught it
stam: when [the mishna] counts the prohibitions of oto veet beno, it does not count foreign prohibitions
stam: wherever there is no oto-veet-beno prohibition it counts foreign prohibitions; wherever there is one, it does not
R' Zeira: leave [the lav of] mechusar zman -- the verse transmuted it into a positive command
[R' Zeira's verse] 'from the eighth day on it shall be accepted' (Lev 22:27) -- from the eighth day yes, before then no: a prohibition that comes from a positive command is a positive command
R' Aptoriki: 'seven days under its mother' -- so the night is fit; 'from the eighth day on it shall be accepted' -- the night is not. How so? the night for consecration, the day for acceptance
stam: another verse is written -- 'so shall you do with your ox, with your sheep' (Ex 22:29)
R' Shimon: a slaughter that is not fit is not called slaughter
Rav Hamnuna: R' Shimon would say -- oto veet beno does not apply to kodashim
the reason: since R' Shimon said an unfit slaughter is not called slaughter, the slaughter of kodashim too is an unfit slaughter
baraita: oto veet beno, kodashim outside -- R' Shimon says: [for] the second [he is] under a prohibition
whatever is fit to come [to the altar] after a time -- [slaughtering it outside] is under a prohibition
R' Shimon: and there is no karet for it
the Sages say: whatever has no karet is not under a prohibition
[Rava] the first was mere killing, the second is fit to be accepted inside -- let him be liable karet too
Rava: [the baraita] is lacking, and this is what it teaches
kodashim, both outside: by the Rabbis the first is punished with karet, the second is unfit and exempt from the prohibition of slaughtering outside
by R' Shimon both are punished with karet
one outside and one inside: by the Rabbis the first is punished with karet, the second is unfit and he is exempt
by R' Shimon the second is fit
one inside and one outside: by the Rabbis the first is fit and he is exempt, the second is unfit and he is exempt
by R' Shimon the second is under a prohibition
Rava: this is what Rav Hamnuna says -- the lashes of oto veet beno do not apply to kodashim
Rava: since as long as the blood is not sprinkled the meat is not permitted, from the moment he slaughters it is an uncertain forewarning
Rava: and an uncertain forewarning is not called a forewarning
Rava: she chullin and her offspring shelamim -- if he slaughtered the chullin and afterwards the shelamim, he is exempt
Rava: shelamim and afterwards chullin -- he is liable
Rava: she chullin and her offspring an olah -- needless to say, if he slaughtered the chullin and afterwards the olah, he is exempt
Rava: but even if he slaughtered the olah and afterwards the chullin, he is exempt
Rava: the first slaughter is not a slaughter subject to eating
R' Yochanan: consumption by the altar is called consumption
[R' Yochanan's verse] 'and if it be at all eaten of the flesh of his peace offering' (Lev 7:18)
the verse speaks of two consumptions: one human consumption and one consumption by the altar
